7.6 — Level Studio I

Paper day is over (7.5); build day is here. Today the sketch becomes tiles, beats become rooms, and by the end of class your cave is WALKABLE from entrance to the boss door — unpolished, ugly, and real.

Studio Brief ~45 min

The contract:

  • All 6 beats of your sketch exist as tiles — entrance to boss door, no gaps
  • Every beat is passable (you do not need it FUN yet — you need it REACHABLE)
  • Enemies/turrets/spikes placed ONLY where the sketch says — resist the urge to sprinkle (sprinkling is what makes levels random; placement is what makes them fair)
  • Ladders work top AND bottom (7.4 solutions applied)
  • Soft gate present if your design has one

Build order (it matters):

  1. Grey-box the FLOOR of the whole cave first — one long walk from entrance to boss door, flat. Run it. The walk is the spine; everything else hangs off it
  2. Add the vertical structure (stairs, walls, ladders) beat by beat. Run between each beat — walk the whole cave every time. The 60-second full walk is your build ritual
  3. Place the threats LAST, from the sketch, with their numbers already chosen (patrol lengths, cooldowns, spike rows). Threats are the most expensive thing to move, so they go in when geometry is stable

Bug Hunt: Studio smells

  1. You cannot make beat 3's jump without the boots. Is that a gate or a mistake? What distinguishes them — a VISIBLE alternative? Mark your sketch.
  2. Your walk ritual discovers a seam stop (7.2 invisible wall) in beat 2. Why is finding it NOW cheap and finding it during a playtest expensive?
  3. An enemy fell through the floor into the void. What did you forget at its spawn point — and why do placed-from-prefab enemies remind you about colliders the hard way?
Checkpoint ~10 min

End-of-studio checks — every one answers to the walk ritual:

Tinker: Close the day

  1. Walk the full cave, out loud, naming each beat as you enter it ("teeth... rest..."). If you cannot name them, the beats are not yet distinct.
  2. Write tomorrow's playtest plan: which beat do you MOST want watched? That beat gets a partner first (7.7).
  3. Commit + push: "7.6a: cave greybox complete, threats placed".

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Walk your whole cave entrance-to-door without bugs stopping you
  • Name each beat as you pass through it
  • Explain why threats go in last and geometry first
  • Have a written playtest plan for tomorrow's audience
